Amasa
uh-MAY-suh
proper noun
From the Hebrew, perhaps “burden” or “a people spared.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Amasa was a kinsman of David, the son of his sister Abigail by Jether the Ishmeelite, and thus cousin to Joab. He rose to prominence as captain of the host under Absalom in the great rebellion against David. When that revolt was crushed and Amasa lay among the defeated, David—seeking to win Judah and to break the proud dominance of Joab—swore to make Amasa captain of the host in Joab’s room continually. Thus a man who had borne the sword against the king was set over the king’s armies, a striking display of David’s mercy and policy together. But Amasa proved slow to gather Judah within the appointed days, and in the pursuit of Sheba the son of Bichri, Joab met him at the great stone in Gibeon. Feigning a kinsman’s greeting, Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him, and with the sword in his other hand smote him in the fifth rib, shedding out his bowels to the ground. So Amasa died in his own blood in the highway, a victim of Joab’s jealous treachery. His brief and bloody career shows how the throne’s favor cannot shield a man from the murderous ambition of the wicked, and how God’s providence threads even kingly mercy and base betrayal toward His own ends.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Absalom’s captain, later made David’s commander, slain treacherously by Joab at the stone in Gibeon.

expand to see more

AMASA, the son of Abigail, David’s sister, by Jether the Ishmeelite, and cousin to Joab.

He was made captain of the host by Absalom in his rebellion against David (2Sa 17:25).

After the revolt David swore to set him over the army in Joab’s room.

He tarried longer than the set time in gathering the men of Judah.

Joab feigned a greeting and slew him in the fifth rib at the great stone in Gibeon (2Sa 20:10).

📖 Key Scripture

2Sa 17:25 — "And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man’s son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab’s mother."

2Sa 19:13 — "And say ye to Amasa, Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab."

2Sa 20:9 — "And Joab said to Amasa, Art thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him."

2Sa 20:10 — "But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Amasa’s end exposes the murderous jealousy that festers when men love power above the king’s peace.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The lesson to recover is the deadliness of ambition that wears the mask of friendship. Joab’s kiss of greeting concealed the dagger of envy; he could not bear to be supplanted, and so he murdered his own kinsman in cold blood. The treachery is named treachery, and the blood of Amasa cried against Joab to David’s last charge.

Amasa also stands as a sober figure of misplaced trust—he took no heed to the sword. The believer is warned to discern the wolf beneath the warm word, and rulers are warned that mercy extended to former rebels must reckon with the jealousy of entrenched men. God’s providence governed even this, yet Joab bore the guilt.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name may carry the sense of a burden borne or a people spared, fitting one caught between rebellion and royal favor.

expand to see more

Amasa — Hebrew, possibly from a root meaning “to bear a burden.”

His father is named both Jether and Ithra, an Ishmeelite or Israelite, in the records.

His mother Abigail was sister to David and to Zeruiah, mother of Joab.

Thus Amasa and Joab were cousins, rivals for the captaincy of the host.

His death at Gibeon is one of three murders David charged against Joab.

Usage

"Amasa took no heed to the sword—a warning against trusting the false embrace of an envious man."

"Like Amasa, the latecomer to duty may find his delay turned to his ruin."

"David’s charge concerning the blood of Amasa pursued Joab to his own end."
